role_context: A PowerShell practitioner at the intermediate level is expected to independently build and maintain production-oriented scripts, advanced functions, and reusable modules that support operational automation, reporting, data processing, and integration with REST APIs or external systems. They should own moderately complex workflows end to end, including parameter design, pipeline behavior, structured object output, safe WhatIf behavior, robust CSV/JSON handling, pagination, authentication, retry logic, and clear failure handling for batch operations. They are expected to make sound implementation choices around time-zone correctness, semantic version comparison, streaming performance, idempotent reruns, and quarantine/archive patterns, while escalating only higher-risk architectural decisions or ambiguous system behaviors to senior engineers. They should also write meaningful Pester tests with mocks, setup logic, tagged runs, and basic performance assertions to validate reliability, correctness, and scalability across thousands of records or files.
questions_prompt:
Please ensure the questions you ask cover the key functional, logical, architectural, implementation, debugging, optimization, review, and problem-solving areas from the competency scope for {name}, matched to {proficiency} proficiency ({yoe} years experience).

Design a bar-raiser style technical assessment prompt for PowerShell intermediate proficiency. The assessment should ask the candidate to solve, fix, build, or review a realistic work item rather than answer trivia or perform configuration lookup. Focus only on applied PowerShell work involving the following topic areas and sub-skills:

- Advanced functions and modules: using advanced function design concepts such as CmdletBinding, parameter attributes, parameter sets, pipeline input with begin/process/end, .psm1 module organization, controlled exports, emitting typed PSCustomObjects, separating data from presentation, and supporting ShouldProcess/-WhatIf with genuinely side-effect-free dry-run behavior.
- Data and time correctness: parsing DateTime values with explicit formats and cultures, handling UTC versus local time, recognizing midnight and DST edge cases, using injectable reference clocks for reliable time logic, parsing and comparing semantic versions, and robustly processing CSV/JSON data including quoted fields, BOMs, malformed rows, and reject/quarantine flows.
- Scale and performance: streaming through the pipeline instead of loading large directories or files fully into memory, using Group-Object or hashtable-based aggregation over large collections, and meeting explicit time budgets across thousands of input files.
- REST APIs and external systems: using Invoke-RestMethod patterns for pagination, authentication headers, and structured payloads; applying bounded retry with exponential backoff; failing fast on 4xx responses versus retrying appropriate 5xx responses; and building summary/report objects for downstream consumption.
- Reliability engineering: distinguishing warnings from terminating errors, isolating per-item failures in batch jobs, designing idempotent re-runs, and using archive/quarantine patterns for safe recovery and repeatability.

This is an intermediate proficiency, so somebody attempting this task has a few years of experience but is not an expert in these domains. Ensure that tasks are around fundamentals, and candidates should be able to finish this within 20 minutes. Let there be multiple ways to achieve the correct outcome — the idea is to see what paths the candidate picks. Make the tasks subjective yet specific and clear in their expected outcomes.

Prefer scenarios that assess understanding of requirements and constraints, reasoning about ambiguous real-world situations, quality of technical decisions and tradeoff analysis, identifying root causes, risks, and edge cases, proposing or implementing pragmatic solutions, and reviewing or improving existing work. The task should involve a realistic scenario such as improving an operational script, designing a safer batch-processing function, reviewing a flawed module function, adding pagination/retry behavior to an API integration, making CSV/JSON ingestion more robust, or optimizing a script that processes many files.

Avoid questions that primarily test testing-framework details, test configuration, tool installation/setup, language/library syntax recall, or pure semantics. Do not ask candidates to memorize exact command switches unless they are naturally part of a practical implementation or review task. Include enough context, sample inputs or flawed snippets if useful, constraints, and expected outcomes so the candidate can reason and produce a concrete answer within the time limit.

The goal is to evaluate applied competence, practical problem-solving, implementation and review ability, sound technical judgment, and the candidate's ability to deliver realistic solutions within the expected time constraints for their proficiency level.
